card: This PR immediately disconnects sockets across Connman, the HTTP server, and other callers when a wait reports an ErrorEvent instead of continuing to read or write. On select()-based platforms (macOS, BSDs, and Windows), peer urgent data triggers an exception event that the node cannot read, leading to continuous thread wakeups and busy looping. This serves as an immediate fix and an alternative to PR #36716 while wider socket polling refactors are explored in issue #36761.
evidence: PR description: 'On select() based platform (BSDs, macOS and Windows), ErrorEvent can be returned if a peer sends us urgent data (we register the exception set because of a Windows quirk). However we can't read that urgent data, and this means we could be continuously woken up.'
problem: When a socket wait returns an ErrorEvent, callers currently continue trying to read or send even if a read was not requested. On select()-based platforms (BSDs, macOS, Windows), peers sending urgent data trigger the exception set; because Bitcoin Core cannot read that urgent data, the thread can be continuously woken up in a busy loop.

risk.why: Mishandling socket error states or disconnect triggers could drop legitimate peer or RPC/HTTP connections prematurely, degrading node connectivity.

scope_notes: Diff was not provided in the input; size is +31/-6 across 6 files touching P2P and HTTP socket event handling.
summary: Instructs socket-event callers (such as Connman and the HTTP server) to stop reading and writing and immediately disconnect when a socket wait operation reports an ErrorEvent. This standardizes error handling across socket polling callers.
uncertainties: Diff was not provided, preventing verification of exact caller modifications and disconnect mechanisms.
